clue.text: Crazy slanderous remarks about celebrity in plant

parts.note: wild means crazy or frenzied

indicators.note: about means the remarks go round the celebrity word, enclosing it

parts.note: mud is slanderous talk, as in mud-slinging
a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: Some gossip about a famous person turns up, oddly, inside a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlock, a yellow-flowered weed of fields, is the common species known by this name, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: With complete authority

parts.note: arrant means complete or utter, as in arrant nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone acts with absolute power.
explanation.definitionFit: A document giving legal power to act, such as for an arrest, is an authority.

clue.text: Runner-up in close race?

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words close race, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A competitor finishes second in a tight contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads like a cryptic definition of a narrowly beaten runner, but the letters are tucked inside 'close race'.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever comes second has failed to win, so the runner-up is the beaten party in the contest.

clue.text: Chef's mixture, notice, taken in by soldier aboard ship?

indicators.note: taken in by means the notice word sits inside the soldier word

parts.note: a marine is a soldier serving aboard a ship
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A cook's concoction and an advertisement are absorbed by a seagoing soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A seasoned liquid in which food is soaked before cooking is a mixture prepared by a cook.

clue.text: Wife turned up, about to hit the roof

indicators.note: about means the reversed title goes round the small word
turned up in a down clue says the title is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Mrs is the title of a wife

explanation.surface: A wife appears and is about to lose her temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' looks like 'on the point of', but 'about' is the container signal and 'to' is plain fodder; 'turned up' gives SRM.
explanation.definitionFit: To rage or rush about angrily is the same as losing one's temper explosively.

clue.text: A storage tower erected to keep produce in citadel

indicators.note: to keep means the A and reversed tower hold the produce word inside
erected in a down clue means the tower's name is set upright, reading upwards

parts.note: a silo is a tower for storing grain
a crop is farm produce

explanation.surface: A farmer puts up a silo to store a harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' turns SILO into OLIS; A and OLIS 'keep' CROP.
explanation.definitionFit: The fortified upper part of an ancient Greek city, notably Athens, is a citadel.

clue.text: Energetic type held up by so many duties

indicators.note: held up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A busy person is delayed by an overwhelming workload.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'held up' reads the letters OMANYD, from 'so many duties', upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirelessly energetic person is called a dynamo, after the electricity generator.

clue.text: Intensive course in hospital in Notts town

indicators.note: in puts the hospital letter inside the town's name

parts.note: Worksop is a market town in Nottinghamshire, abbreviated Notts, in the English Midlands

explanation.surface: A training course is held at a hospital in a Midlands town.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, intensive session of study or training on a topic is a familiar sense of the word.

clue.text: Fox coming from marshy land with endless boldness

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land, as in East Anglia

indicators.note: endless says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: neck is boldness or cheek

explanation.surface: A cheeky fox emerges from the marshes.
explanation.definitionFit: The small desert species with very large ears is a kind of fox, found in North Africa.

clue.text: Ice, briefly, over Irish lake

indicators.note: briefly says the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: ice is a cold aloofness of manner, which is reserve
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone notes ice forming over a lake in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ice' is not frozen water here but coolness of manner, RESERVE; 'briefly' drops its last letter to give RESERV.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-made lake that stores a water supply is called by this name, so the word fits a lake.

clue.text: Snare, one so devilish

indicators.note: devilish suggests something wicked and twisted, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A trap is described as particularly fiendish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devilish' rearranges the letters of ONE SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop of cord that tightens when pulled is a snare used to catch animals.

clue.text: Initial letters from a friend, male

parts.note: a crony is a close friend

explanation.surface: Someone receives a note signed only with initials from a male friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed from the first letters of other words, such as NATO, is built from initial letters.

clue.text: Persistently question family that supplies fruit

parts.note: to pump someone is to question them persistently for information
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: Someone grills the relatives who run a fruit stall.
explanation.definitionFit: The large orange gourd is botanically a fruit, the fleshy seed-bearing part of the plant.

clue.text: Time to study factory's routine

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it, as at university
a mill is a factory; the 's stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition

explanation.surface: Studying at the factory is time-consuming drudgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a monotonous round of repetitive work is likened to the exercise machine, so it means a dull routine.

clue.text: Feeling upon receiving Charlie's messaging symbol

indicators.note: upon receiving means the feeling word takes in the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: an emotion is a feeling
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone feels emotional when a message from Charlie arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiley face or similar pictogram used in texts to show mood is a symbol used in messaging.

clue.text: Usually popular army officer

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a general is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: A senior army commander is generally well liked.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means as a rule or for the most part, which is what usually means.

clue.text: Fashionable greeting in Conservative clubs

indicators.note: in places the greeting word inside the pair of single letters

parts.note: C is the card-playing abbreviation for clubs
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A stylish hello is exchanged in Tory clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant and stylish, borrowed from French, the word is a synonym of fashionable.

clue.text: One making toast, professional model

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a poser is someone who poses, as a model does

explanation.surface: A professional model raises a glass at a dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' is a speech with raised glasses, not grilled bread.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who formally proposes a toast at a dinner is the one making it.

clue.text: Give up 'Decline and Fall'?

definitions.meaning: to give up a habit or plan is to abandon it
a decline or a fall in prices is a fall downwards

explanation.surface: Someone abandons reading Gibbon's 'Decline and Fall'.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted title evokes Gibbon's history of Rome, but it is simply two words meaning a downward fall.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to abandon something and a decrease or descent.

clue.text: Menial servant died — Dickens character

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies
Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: A lowly servant in a Dickens novel dies.
explanation.definitionFit: A person made to do hard, dull work is a drudge, a menial servant.

clue.text: Top grub, as cooked here?

indicators.note: cooked suggests ingredients being worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fine food is prepared on the premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges TOP GRUB AS; the whole clue also describes the place.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub known for serving high-quality food is where top grub is cooked.

clue.text: Two articles supporting bishop? Like crazy

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means the articles sit beneath the bishop letter

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: two says the article is taken twice

parts.note: an is an indefinite article
as means like

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether two pieces of writing back a bishop, and is told it's crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, to go bananas is to go mad, so the word means crazy.

clue.text: Talk idly having small drink after work

indicators.note: after means the small drink is placed following the work word

parts.note: go means work or function, as a machine does
a sip is a small drink

explanation.surface: Colleagues chat over a quick drink after work.
explanation.definitionFit: To chatter about other people's affairs is idle talk, so the verb means talk idly.

clue.text: Mythical creature, fabulous bird, displayed over in a French home

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: in puts the turned bird inside the word for home

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: displayed over says the bird's name is shown turned round

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: A mythical beast and a legendary bird appear in a French house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed over' gives COR; 'home' is the word IN, as in 'staying in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse with a single horn is a creature of myth and legend.

clue.text: Severe blow, printing error involving house name

indicators.note: involving means the error word wraps round the house abbreviation

parts.note: a typo is a printing error

explanation.surface: A misprinted house name comes as a nasty shock.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical cyclone of great violence is a severe blow, blow meaning a gale.

clue.text: Prison sentence beginning to skate by

parts.note: doing time is serving a prison sentence

indicators.note: beginning to says take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A prisoner's sentence starts to slip by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is the multiplication sense, as in a room four by five.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic and measurement, multiplied by and 'times' are the same, as in three by four.

clue.text: Nothing new working under single bulb

indicators.note: under in a down clue means the working word comes below the single one

parts.note: O is zero, nothing
I is the Roman numeral one, single
on means working, as a switched-on machine is

explanation.surface: A new light bulb is switched on beneath a single lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bulb' is the vegetable, not a light.
explanation.definitionFit: The layered vegetable grows as a bulb underground, so it is an example of a bulb.

clue.text: Bring in grand polar explorer

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
James Clark Ross explored both the Arctic and the Antarctic

explanation.surface: An expedition recruits a distinguished explorer of the poles.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn a total amount before deductions is to bring it in as income.

clue.text: On crusade to get pardon

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a mission is a crusade or campaign

explanation.surface: A crusader seeks absolution for sins.
explanation.definitionFit: Forgiveness of sins or cancellation of a penalty is a pardon, an older sense of the word.

clue.text: Initially managed well, nursed by friends in US city

indicators.note: nursed by means held inside the arms of the friends word

parts.note: pals are friends

indicators.note: initially says take the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: a spring is a well, a natural water source

explanation.surface: Someone who is unwell recovers thanks to friends' care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' gives M from 'managed'; M and SPRING are 'nursed by' PALS.
explanation.definitionFit: The resort in the Californian desert is a city in the United States.
